stages.title: Advanced linguistics and grammar
stages.hook: Why can "Я писал письмо" and "Я написал письмо" both translate as "I wrote a letter", yet not mean the same?
explain: Russian is a synthetic, fusional language: endings carry several meanings at once. Verbs have aspect (вид). The imperfective (писать) presents an action as a process, repeated or without a limit, while the perfective (написать) presents it as a completed whole with a result. Я писал письмо says that I was engaged in writing, while Я написал письмо says that the letter is finished.

Aspect pairs are formed by prefixes (делать – сделать), by suffixes (решать – решить) or by a different root (говорить – сказать). Word order in Russian is guided by information structure: known information (theme) comes first and new information (rheme) at the end, so Книгу купил брат and Брат купил книгу differ in emphasis.
stages.mnemonic: Process or result: the aspect pair is a camera and a photograph.
sentences: I was reading the book but did not finish it.
The case expresses the role of a word.

gq.q: What does Я написал письмо express that Я писал письмо does not?
gq.why: The perfective presents the action as a completed whole.

gq.q: Which pair is an aspect pair with different roots?

panel.q: What do the sentences Книгу купил брат and Брат купил книгу differ in?
o: Information structure and emphasis, not basic meaning
panel.why: Case endings fix roles, so order marks emphasis.

panel.q: Why is Russian called fusional?
o: One ending expresses several categories such as case, number and gender together
panel.why: The ending -ой in большой marks gender, number and case at once.

panel.q: Why can a prefix change aspect and meaning at the same time?
o: Some prefixes add a result or direction as well as perfectivity
panel.why: Prefixed perfectives may add nuances, e.g. про- or до-.

teach.model: Russian is a fusional language. Verb aspect contrasts process (imperfective) with completed result (perfective). Word order depends on information structure: known first, new last.

trip.prompt: Read the Slavic section and find one aspect pair with an example.

stages.title: Historical development of the language
stages.hook: Why does Russian have two words, город and град, for "city"?
explain: Russian belongs to the East Slavic branch of the Slavic family, within the Indo-European languages. It developed from Old East Slavic (древнерусский язык), the language of Kievan Rus'. The Cyrillic script came with Christianity, and Church Slavonic became the language of the Church and of literature.

Church Slavonic left many words in Russian, creating pairs such as город and град, ворота and врата, голова and глава, where the Slavonic form often has a more elevated meaning. Peter I introduced a simplified civil script in 1708, and the orthographic reform of 1918 removed letters such as ять (ѣ) and a final hard sign.
stages.mnemonic: Старое слово pair: the Church Slavonic twin sounds more solemn.
sentences: Russian belongs to the Slavic languages.
The orthographic reform took place in 1918.
The chronicle is an important source.

gq.q: To which branch of Slavic does Russian belong?
gq.why: Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian are East Slavic.

gq.q: What explains pairs such as город and град?
gq.why: Slavonic forms entered Russian with Church texts.

panel.q: Why do Church Slavonic forms often sound more elevated?
o: They came through religious and literary language
panel.why: Their stylistic value comes from their original use.

panel.q: What did the 1918 reform change?
o: It removed several letters and simplified spelling
panel.why: The reform removed letters like ѣ.

panel.q: What is the value of a chronicle for linguists?
o: It preserves early written forms of the language
panel.why: Early texts show earlier stages of the language.

teach.model: Russian is East Slavic and developed from Old East Slavic. Church Slavonic influenced its vocabulary, giving pairs like город and град. Peter I and the 1918 reform simplified the script.

points.ask: What was the role of Church Slavonic?

trip.prompt: Find the periods of development and list three.

stages.title: Literature and cultural discourse
stages.hook: In Soviet times some books were copied by hand and passed between friends. What was this called?
explain: Russian literary history is often divided into periods. The Golden Age (золотой век) of the early 19th century is linked with Pushkin, and the Silver Age (серебряный век) of the early 20th century with poets such as Anna Akhmatova, Alexander Blok and Marina Tsvetaeva. The intelligentsia (интеллигенция) is a social group with a strong cultural role.

In the Soviet Union, texts that the censors did not allow could circulate in typed or handwritten copies called samizdat (самиздат). Толстые журналы (thick journals) published novels and essays and shaped public debate. Bulgakov's Мастер и Маргарита was written in the 1930s but published only in the 1960s.
stages.mnemonic: Golden for Pushkin, Silver for Akhmatova, samizdat for hand-passed pages.
sentences: The Silver Age gave Russian poetry many names.

gq.q: Who is a poet of the Silver Age?
gq.why: Akhmatova belongs to the early 20th century.

o: Self-published copies of texts not approved by the censors

panel.q: Why was literature so important in Russian public life?
o: Writers often discussed moral and social questions that were hard to debate openly
panel.why: Literature served as a forum for ideas.

panel.q: What does the delayed publication of Мастер и Маргарита show?
o: Censorship could delay major works for decades
panel.why: The novel appeared long after it was written.

panel.q: What is a canon?
o: A set of works regarded as the most important
panel.why: The canon is shaped by tradition and criticism.

teach.model: Russian literature is divided into the Golden Age and the Silver Age. The intelligentsia played a major cultural role. Samizdat circulated unapproved texts in the Soviet Union.

trip.prompt: Read the first section and note how texts were copied.

stages.title: Advanced academic writing
stages.hook: A Russian scientific article begins with an abstract. Which questions must the abstract answer?
explain: Academic Russian writing follows conventions. A thesis or article opens with an аннотация (abstract), then states the актуальность (relevance of the topic), the цель работы (aim), the объект (object) and предмет (subject) of research, and the научная новизна (novelty). Methods and results follow, and a библиография lists the sources.

A dash often replaces "is": Цель работы — проанализировать данные. Style is impersonal, passive and precise: В работе использованы следующие методы. Hedges mark uncertainty: по-видимому (apparently), возможно (possibly). References use phrases like см. (see) and Ср. (compare).
stages.mnemonic: Relevance, aim, object, subject, novelty: the five doors of an introduction.
sentences: The aim of the work is to analyse the data.
The novelty consists in a new approach.
The following methods are used in the work.

gq.q: What does the dash in Цель работы — проанализировать данные replace?
o: The omitted present tense of "to be"
gq.why: The dash marks omission of "is" before an infinitive or noun.

gq.q: Which section states why the topic matters?
gq.why: Актуальность justifies the choice of topic.

panel.q: Why distinguish объект from предмет исследования?
o: The object is the broader phenomenon and the subject is the aspect actually studied
panel.why: Russian academic convention separates field and focus.

panel.q: Why do academic texts use hedges like по-видимому?
o: They show appropriate caution about conclusions
panel.why: Caution reflects the limits of evidence.

panel.q: Why is a bibliography necessary?
o: It lets readers verify sources and acknowledges others' work
panel.why: Transparent sourcing is basic scholarly ethics.

teach.model: An academic text states актуальность, цель, объект, предмет and научная новизна, uses an impersonal style and hedging, and lists sources in a bibliography. A dash may replace "is".

trip.prompt: Read the page on abstracts and write a 3-sentence abstract about a topic you like.

stages.title: Professional translation
stages.hook: A sign says "Не курить" with an infinitive. How should a translator render it into English?
explain: Professional translation means producing a text that works in the target culture. Signs in Russian often use the infinitive: Не курить corresponds to "No smoking". A literal "Not to smoke" would be wrong. This is a translation shift (переводческая трансформация).

Professionals use a glossary (глоссарий) for consistency, ensure correct collocations (устойчивые сочетания), localise units and dates (локализация) and finish with proofreading (вычитка). Names are transliterated by a stated system, so Достоевский appears as Dostoevsky or Dostoyevsky depending on the system. Pragmatics matters: the text must have the same effect on its reader as the original.
stages.mnemonic: Same effect, different words: translation is rebuilding, not copying.
sentences: The translator must know the terminology.

gq.q: How is the Russian sign Не курить best rendered in English?
gq.why: Translators match the conventional sign form of the target language.

gq.q: Why does a professional keep a glossary?
o: To keep terms consistent across a text
gq.why: Consistency is a mark of quality.

panel.q: Why do names like Достоевский have several English spellings?
panel.why: Transliteration conventions differ.

panel.q: What is the aim of localisation?
o: To make a text fit the target culture, including units, dates and conventions
panel.why: Localisation goes beyond translating words.

panel.q: Which is a typical translation shift from Russian to English?
o: Passive impersonal Russian turned into an active English sentence
panel.why: English prefers active forms, so shifts are common.

teach.model: A professional translator aims for the same effect on the reader. Use glossaries for consistency, convention-appropriate forms like No smoking for Не курить, localisation and proofreading.

points.ask: What is the aim of translation?
How do I keep terms consistent?

trip.prompt: Read about translation shifts and write one Russian-English example.

stages.title: Interpretation of complex communication
stages.hook: A friend says "Тут не жарко?" while looking at the window. What does the friend really want?
explain: Interpreting complex communication means reading beyond the words. Тут не жарко? can be a request to open the window, an example of indirect speech. Implied meaning (подтекст), hints (намёки), irony (ирония), euphemism (эвфемизм) and allegory (иносказание) all need context, intonation and shared knowledge.

Polysemy (многозначность) means that one word has several senses, and context chooses the right one. Irony is often signalled by intonation: Ну, спасибо тебе большое! after a spilled drink means the opposite of thanks. Euphemisms soften sensitive facts: скончался for "died". Non-verbal signals (невербальные сигналы) such as gestures and silence also carry meaning.
stages.mnemonic: The sentence says one thing; the situation says another.
sentences: The speaker hints at something else.
Irony is often expressed by intonation.

gq.q: A friend spills tea on your book and you say "Ну, спасибо тебе большое!" with falling, sharp intonation. What do you convey?
gq.why: Intonation turns the words into their opposite.

gq.q: What is скончался in a news report?
gq.why: It is a formal, softer way to say died.

panel.q: What does the question Тут не жарко? typically communicate?
o: An indirect request, e.g. to open the window
panel.why: Pragmatic meaning exceeds literal meaning.

panel.q: Why does an interpreter need cultural knowledge?
o: Meaning often depends on shared background, not words
panel.why: Cultural context decides implied meaning.

panel.q: How does polysemy create difficulty?
o: One word may have several senses, so context must choose
panel.why: The interpreter selects the sense from context.

teach.model: Meaning can go beyond words: subtext, hints, irony, euphemism and indirect requests. Use context, intonation and cultural knowledge. Polysemy means that one word has several senses.

trip.prompt: Read about implicature and find an English example of an indirect request.

stages.title: Language variation and dialectology
stages.hook: Is there one "correct" Russian, or many varieties? Linguists study this question.
explain: Dialectology studies regional varieties (диалекты, говоры). The standard language (литературный язык) is based on educated Moscow speech, with codified rules of spelling and pronunciation. Russian dialects are traditionally divided into northern, southern and transitional groups. Northern speech keeps a clear о in unstressed syllables (оканье), while southern and standard speech use аканье.

Social varieties also exist. Просторечие is non-standard everyday speech, жаргон is slang used by a group, and professional jargon belongs to a trade. Speakers move between varieties depending on situation. Russian is also spoken in many countries, where it contacts other languages and develops local features.
stages.mnemonic: North says "o", south says "a", the standard picks "a".
sentences: The standard language is based on Moscow speech.
Slang is used in a group.

gq.q: What is the standard literary Russian traditionally based on?
gq.why: Standard pronunciation norms derive from Moscow speech.

o: Unstressed о is pronounced as a
The letter о is a consonant
Unstressed о is pronounced as о
gq.why: Okanye is typical of northern dialects.

panel.q: Why do speakers switch between varieties?
o: Different situations call for different registers
panel.why: Style shifting is a normal feature of language.

panel.q: What is the difference between жаргон and диалект?
o: Жаргон is tied to a social group and диалект is tied to a place
panel.why: Sociolects differ from regional dialects.

panel.q: Why does Russian outside Russia develop local features?
o: Contact with other languages influences vocabulary and usage
panel.why: Language contact produces variation.

teach.model: Dialectology studies regional and social varieties. The standard is based on Moscow speech. Northern dialects keep okanye and southern ones use akanye. Жаргон is group slang.

points.ask: What is the standard based on?

trip.prompt: Find a map of dialect groups and name the three main ones.

stages.title: Specialised scientific or technical language
stages.hook: Scientific Russian packs a lot into long chains of nouns in the genitive. What does "скорость изменения температуры" mean?
explain: Scientific and technical Russian uses precise terms and compact structures. A chain of genitives builds a complex idea: скорость изменения температуры means "the rate of change of temperature". Many terms come from Greek and Latin, such as алгоритм, молекула and эксперимент, while others are Russian: погрешность (error margin), скорость (speed).

Formulas and units follow set patterns. Statements are impersonal: Эксперимент подтвердил формулу. Dmitri Mendeleev published the periodic table in 1869, and Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space in 1961. Scientific texts avoid emotion and ambiguity, and numbers are written with a decimal comma: 3,5.
stages.mnemonic: Read a genitive chain from the right: temperature, of change, rate.
sentences: The speed of light is constant.

gq.why: Russian uses a comma as the decimal separator.
It is the possible error in a measurement.

panel.q: Why are genitive chains typical of scientific Russian?
o: They express relations between concepts compactly
panel.why: Genitive noun phrases pack information.

panel.q: Why do scientific terms often come from Greek and Latin?
o: These classical languages supply an international vocabulary
panel.why: Shared roots help international communication.

panel.q: Why must scientific language be unambiguous?
o: Results need to be reproduced and understood exactly
panel.why: Precision supports reproducibility.

teach.model: Scientific Russian is compact and precise, with genitive chains like скорость изменения температуры. Many terms come from Greek and Latin. It uses an impersonal style and a decimal comma.

trip.prompt: Read about Mendeleev and note the year of the table.

stages.title: Integrated proficiency project
stages.hook: You must present a small research project in Russian. Which steps bring your whole language knowledge together?
explain: An integrated project combines reading, research, writing and speaking. Choose a topic, collect sources, state the aim and main finding (основной результат), explain the limitations (ограничения) and suggest a recommendation (рекомендация). Justify claims with evidence (доказательства) and acknowledge other views.

In the final presentation use signposts (Итак, Предлагаю рассмотреть...), a clear structure, accurate cases and aspect, and an appropriate register. Be ready for questions with phrases like Позвольте уточнить... (Let me clarify...). Peer review (рецензирование) improves quality: invite comments and revise.
stages.mnemonic: Topic, evidence, result, limits, recommendation: a project in five steps.
sentences: The main result is confirmed by the data.
The limitations of the study are described below.
I propose to consider another approach.

gq.q: Which phrase politely asks to clarify?
gq.why: Позвольте уточнить is a polite formula.

gq.q: Why state the limitations of a study?
o: To show honestly how far the conclusions can be trusted

panel.q: What does peer review contribute?
o: Independent feedback that improves accuracy and clarity
panel.why: Review catches errors and gaps.

panel.q: Which order best fits a project report?
panel.why: The logical flow helps the reader.

panel.q: A listener challenges your claim. What is a good response?
o: Give evidence and acknowledge valid doubts
panel.why: Argument rests on evidence and openness.

teach.model: A project combines reading, research, writing and speaking. State the aim, main result, limitations and recommendation, justify claims with evidence and use a suitable register. Invite peer review.

points.ask: How do I improve my project?

trip.prompt: Read about the research process and list its steps.
